title: TAPE WOBBLE -- stereo analog tape wow, flutter and saturation

sections.heading: USING IT
lines: AUDIO: drop a sound file into the player and play it. Turn on audio with the speaker button.
WOW Rate / Depth: slow pitch drift (0.1-6 Hz).
FLUTTER Rate / Depth: fast pitch wobble (3-30 Hz).
TAPE Drift: random slow wander, like old or worn tape.
TAPE Drive: tape saturation for warmth.
EQ HF Cut: high-frequency rolloff (4-15 kHz).
EQ Gain / Freq: low 'head bump' boost (0-6 dB at 60-200 Hz).
OUTPUT Spread: stereo difference between left and right.
VISUALIZATION: dry input, wet output and the combined pitch-modulation signal.

sections.heading: HOW IT WORKS
lines: One gen~ codebox does all the processing: saturation, then a short modulated delay.
The delay time is moved by wow (sine), flutter (3 harmonics) and a random drift.
A low peaking EQ and a lowpass then shape the tone before the dry/wet mix.
p param-routing turns the dials into gen~ parameter messages.
